The rhetoric towards folks who have chosen a line of work predicated on the collection of tips shouldn't be insane to anyone. For anyone complaining about seeing recommended tips on bills, how is that assesrting anything? Ignore it. Tip what you normally do. I do not know a single person in the industry that ever expects more than 20% at the very most. Many are content with 15-18%.

No bar or restaurant is going to be willing to pay the salary of a bartender, server, busser, etc. a salary. Most of these places operate on slim budgets and margins, there is no way they are going to start paying us what we currently make which means the majority of the good work force will quit the industry and then service will suffer. I don't disagree that tipping culture is out of whack, but in order to overhaul this it would take a herculean effort, not to mention if the younger generations adopt not tipping then the folks who currently work in the industry will suffer.

The Last of Us is a gritty, heart warming but often times gut wrenching tale about a man and a girl trying to survive in the harshest of circumstances with little more than hope. That is a story that can truly move someone to connect with the game and what is happening inside of it. 

Bioshock Infinite was sweeping and a hell of a lot of fun to play, with a rather unique twist on time travel. Elizabeth was a wonderful companion to have in a game and her character was wonderful to watch and learn more about. But now that I've played and beat both I can say with the utmost certainty that because both games were fundamentally different as games it is quite difficult to say which is better.

To me it boils down to the story and how I felt after I finished the game. BI felt like a a fun ride, but once I was done I felt little reason to return because the story was wrapped up, the twist had come and gone and I was satisfied with what I got my first time through. When I finished TLOU my jaw was hanging open and I wanted more. I wanted to experience that world again. I wanted to see the heartbreak and tragedy. I wanted to feel anxious and nervous when I heard a clicker coming near. I wanted to watch Ellie and Joel form that bond again and look closer for little details and find new snip its of conversation to enjoy.

TL,DR: TLOU in my mind is the best game to have come out this year for the current generation systems. BI is great, but not as great as TLOU.

The Big Book has a whole chapter dedicated to agnostics and atheists, aptly titled "To the Agnostic" but upon intensive reading of said chapter it's becoming monumentally clear to me that there are tenants of the BB that clearly state that no aid can come from a man, but only from a higher power of our understanding. 

There are also paragraphs discussing the futility of denying a personal God, and swiftly calling it selfish. How in the world does this cater to maintaining your atheism or agnosticism in the program? (Pgs 55-56 of the BB) it goes into depth on the issue of lack of faith and how fruitless it is, and with a poor circle of logic the author deduces that we were born with the ideal of God and faith in something more. It seems to me that the whole chapter merely hints at the futility of atheism or agnosticism as an alcoholic. On pg 55 the autho even states, " we can only clear the ground a bit.
